prerequisites: Basic knowledge of materials science as taught in the course "Introduction to Materials Science" (H01D0A).

learning_outcomes.text: Introduce the student to the world of technical ceramics, glass, and glass-ceramics.
Study the characteristic bonds in ceramics and document the structure of oxides, silicates, interstitial alloys, and covalent non-oxides.
Explain the importance of structural point defects and non-stoichiometry for diffusion, sintering behavior, and functional properties.

Study fracture toughness, strength, stiffness, hardness, and thermal stresses in ceramics and ceramic composites, as well as design-related aspects such as Weibull statistics, subcritical crack growth, and testing of ceramics.
Achieve a deeper knowledge regarding the correlations between microstructure and properties of different ceramic material classes.
Introduce and illustrate the possible production processes for technical ceramics and the various characteristic steps in this often complex process.

syllabus_topics: Bonds in ceramics and structure of oxide ceramics (oxides, silicates)
Interstitial alloys and covalent non-oxides (carbides, borides, nitrides, SiN4, SiC, C, B4C, …)
Structural defects and diffusion (point defects, diffusion, oxidation/reduction, non-stoichiometry)
Mechanical properties (E, HV, KIC, s, CTE, thermal shocks, residual stresses, etc.)
Designing with ceramics (Weibull statistics, strength-probability-time diagrams, subcritical crack growth)
Three practice sessions on the lecture material.
assessment_rules: The assessment is an oral exam with written preparation. The evaluation characteristics and determination of the final result for the second examination opportunity are identical to those of the first examination opportunity.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
